deep_dive.title: Select, Compress, Reinvest: A Controlled Study of Visual-Token Allocation in Long-Video MLLMs
deep_dive.abstract: Long-video language models cannot look at every frame: an hour sampled once per second is 3,600 images, and a system keeps only a small fixed slice of that pool. Which frames survive that slice is usually treated as a preprocessing detail; we test whether it should be. Published selectors make the comparison hard because they change the frame scorer, the prompt boundary, the resolution policy, and the answering model all at once. We hold each fixed and vary one decision at a time: selection, spatial compression, and reinvestment of the savings, across six training-free selection rules, three long-video benchmarks, and two answering models. Selection is the largest single lever: on LongVideoBench's hour-long bin, eight query-selected frames beat sixteen uniformly spaced ones by 6.9 points, and Orthogonal Matching Pursuit, an unmodified decades-old sparse-approximation algorithm, matches or comes within a point of every purpose-built selector we compare it against, across all three benchmarks. Compression is close to free: halving each frame's spatial budget at fixed timestamps costs at most 0.44 points. Reinvestment is where that budget turns back into accuracy: spending the freed tokens on twice as many compressed frames, at a measured cost no higher than the original eight, returns a further two to three points; compression only pays off once its savings are spent this way. Along the way, an implementation bug in our own AKS baseline and a 0.07 to 3.74 point gap between two harnesses running the same published rules at the same budget show why these comparisons need to happen inside one controlled harness rather than across papers.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: A controlled study of visual-token allocation in long-video MLLMs, isolating selection, spatial compression, and reinvestment decisions. Selection is the largest lever; query-selective frame allocation improves long-video benchmark performance.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 长视频多模态大模型只能从海量候选中保留少量视觉令牌,而帧选择往往被当成预处理细节。该论文固定分辨率策略、提示边界与回答模型,单独改变帧选择、空间压缩和节省预算的再投资三个变量,在六个免训练选择规则、三个长视频基准和两个回答模型上进行受控评测。结果发现选择是影响最大的单点决策,在LongVideoBench小时级片段上,查询相关的选择显著提升准确率。该研究为长视频MLLM中减少视觉令牌数量提供了系统性的实证指导。

quick_skim.title: Tensor Methods for Language Models: From Token Representation to Training, Adaptation, Inference, Compression, and Interpretability
quick_skim.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are built from structured high-dimensional objects such as token representations, weights, adaptation updates, caches, and activations, whose multilinear structure is underexploited by the conventional matrix-centric view. Tensor decompositions and tensor networks provide a principled algebraic language for this structure, yet the literature often treats them as isolated compression mechanisms. This survey organizes tensor methods for LLMs through two complementary views: a seven-stage lifecycle taxonomy covering tokenization, embeddings, pre-training, adaptation, compression, inference, and interpretability, and a component view covering embeddings, attention, and feed-forward networks. We provide unified notation and theoretical foundations, analyze tensorization strategies for individual Transformer components, and compare methods at each lifecycle stage while making differences in evaluation protocols and model scales explicit. We further connect tensor methods to neighboring efficiency techniques and probabilistic tensor networks. Finally, we synthesize open challenges and introduce $ρ_{\rm gap}$, a metric for the compression-realization gap between theoretical memory reduction and measured system-level speedup. By treating tensorization as a common structural principle, the survey provides a structured entry point to tensorized language models and clarifies when parameter savings can plausibly translate into memory efficiency, computational efficiency, or interpretability. The GitHub page dedicated to this paper is accessible at \href{https://github.com/ma-tt-a/awesome-tensor-methods-for-llms}{this https URL}.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: A survey organizing tensor decomposition and tensor network methods across the full LLM lifecycle, covering token representation, training, adaptation, compression, inference, and interpretability, with a component-level view.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有文献常将张量分解等压缩手段当作孤立机制，缺少对LLM全生命周期张量方法的系统梳理。本文用七阶段生命周期与组件双视角组织综述，覆盖词元表示、预训练、适配、压缩、推理与可解释性。指出张量网络与低秩张量分解可统一描述和压缩权重、激活与适配更新，为高效压缩与适配提供通用代数工具，有助于按需选择张量压缩方案。
quick_skim.llm_tldr: 现有文献常将张量分解等压缩手段当作孤立机制，缺少对LLM全生命周期张量方法的系统梳理。本文用七阶段生命周期与组件双视角组织综述，覆盖词元表示、预训练、适配、压缩、推理与可解释性。指出张量网络与低秩张量分解可统一描述和压缩权重、激活与适配更新，为高效压缩与适配提供通用代数工具，有助于按需选择张量压缩方案。
quick_skim.matched_query_text: Papers central to 围绕 LLM/VLM 高效压缩与适配的研究检索关键词, especially work that connects or combines: post-training quantization techniques for large language models including GPTQ AWQ SmoothQuant and OmniQuant; joint quantization and low-rank adaptation for memory efficient fine-tuning of large models; applying orthogonal rotation or Hadamard transforms to reduce outlier effects in weight quantization; reducing the number of visual tokens in vision language models through pruning and merging; compressing video tokens while preserving temporal grounding and event detection; quantization sensitivity of visual and textual modalities in vision language models; How does orthogonal rotation affect the low rank structure of quantization error in large language models?; Can low rank adapters reconstruct quantization error after rotation better than before rotation?; What is the interaction between visual token pruning and post training quantization in vision language models?; How can we preserve temporal information when merging video tokens for video understanding models?.
